says: The first anaesthetic delivers 400, 400, 125 and 125 millilitres of sevoflurane vapour in its first thirty minutes, then none at the concentration 0 for the 10 minutes that the last readings stand, so 1050 millilitres of vapour, 5.25 of liquid and 2.625 kilograms of carbon dioxide equivalent over 40 minutes; desflurane has no factor and no row. The anaesthetic with no stop delivers 50 millilitres of vapour over 5 minutes. In the third, the only concentration is ten minutes old when the flow is first charted, so nothing is counted.
